newsitem.title: UK: House of Fraser says current sales growing.
newsitem.headline: House of Fraser says current sales growing.

text.p: Troubled stores group House of Fraser Plc announced a hefty loss on Thursday, but said sales were up in the current year as it tries to get back into fashion with its customers.
"Sales in the early weeks of the new financial year have been up to expectations with like-for-like growth recorded in both own-bought and concession sales," the company said in a statement.
It said it was particularly encouraged by a "continuing strong performance" from its store in Leeds, which was refurbished last year.

"The board is confident that the actions taken to strategically refocus the business, including the launch of new ranges, coupled with improvements in operational efficiency and customer service, will provide a strong platform for sustained growth in the years ahead," it said.

The group reported a pretax loss after exceptionals of 38.4 million pounds ($62.3 million) on sales of 781.4 million pounds in the year to January 25, compared with a profit of 14.3 million pounds on sales of 748.9 million pounds in the previous year.

The result included 53.2 million pounds in exceptional charges for selling three stores and overhauling its 51 others, as well as taking a 22 million pounds hit for selling off old "off-strategy" stock.

Underlying profits were marginally up at 14.8 million pounds, compared with 14 million pounds last time, which was in line with market forecasts, as was the unchanged dividend payout of 5.5 pence for the year.

The company said like-for-like sales were up 6.3 percent last year and concession sales were up 15.8 percent while the group's sales of its own merchandise was up 2.5 percent. But it said the level of discounting required to clear old stock resulted in "poor gross profit margins (of 31.5 percent)."
